:::{#def-matrix-condition-number}
#### Condition number of a matrix

The **condition number** of an $n \times p$ [matrix](linear-algebra-matrices.qmd#def-matrix) $\matr{A}$
is the [ratio](algebra-sums.qmd#def-ratio) of its largest to its smallest [singular value](#def-singular-values),
counting all $\min(n, p)$ [singular values](#def-singular-values) of $\matr{A}$, zeros included
(@rem-svd-zero-singular-values)
[@wikipedia_condition_number]:

$$
\condnum(\matr{A}) \eqdef \frac{\singval_{\max}}{\singval_{\min}} = \frac{\singval_1}{\singval_{\min(n,p)}}.
$$

This generalizes @def-condition-number,
which covers [positive definite matrices](linear-algebra-special-matrices.qmd#def-positive-definite).
For a nonzero matrix, $\condnum(\matr{A}) \ge 1$.
When the columns of a tall matrix $\matr{A}$ ($n \ge p$) are [linearly dependent](linear-algebra-subspaces.qmd#def-linearly-independent),
its smallest singular value is $0$,
and $\condnum(\matr{A}) = \infty$.

:::
